physical.devices: Samsung SM-A266B Android 16 and itel S667LN Android 13; release APK installed with app data retained
physical.pairedCue: On the shared router, the approved itel operator was granted control and sent AMEN successfully with the LED sign offline. Host state and the mobile stage display received AMEN.
physical.pairedRecovery: Disabled itel Wi-Fi for more than 12 seconds. Its countdown froze, command buttons and private notes were removed, and host regained control. Re-enabling Wi-Fi automatically resumed the approved session without another approval dialog or control regrant.
physical.stageMode: Joining as Stage display forced landscape immersive output. AMEN scrolled. Tap revealed overview/Leave tools, and leaving returned to ordinary portrait UI. Enlarged final typography was additionally reviewed in the fullscreen golden and tested for fit.
physical.ledRecovery: Samsung returned to the W2 hotspot and reauthenticated using remembered credentials. During a new Quick rehearsal countdown, Wi-Fi was disabled from 02:08:35 to approximately 02:08:57 local time. The app detected disconnection, automatically reconnected and restored the lower current time against the original deadline. Subsequent warning and countdown uploads were acknowledged; this check used app/controller evidence, not an optical observation.
physical.explicitDisconnect: After explicit Disconnect, the app remained disconnected despite available sign Wi-Fi, including across an APK upgrade/app restart.
physical.administration: While connected to sign Wi-Fi, authenticated, ended and not sharing, the panel showed Ready to manage this W2 controller. Read Wi-Fi name requested foreground Android location permission and displayed the correct sign SSID. Aligned Open Wi-Fi and Connection details shortcuts opened their destinations.
physical.administrationWrites: No Wi-Fi name, Wi-Fi password, device password, scan settings or firmware were changed. Setter acknowledgement and reconnection still require controlled tests with intentional new values.
physical.startConfirmation: Final short confirmation observed on Samsung: Start the countdown on GloryArenaTimer. Hardware limits/checklist removed.
physical.blankAfterEnd: After End service, Blank screen and Unblank screen were available, confirmed in sequence and returned the end output. No service restart was required.
physical.printing: After End service, Print Service opened Android printing with Include church banner checked and private notes unchecked. Saved a fresh one-page A4 PDF and rendered it for visual review: cropped banner, dark gradient, legible headings and clean rundown. The personal photo/PDF remains outside the repository.
physical.network: Sign hotspot still prevents phone-to-phone pairing; both-phone tests used a normal router. Router-only pairing does not create a route to the sign.
physical.postTest: Sharing stopped, test services ended, peer left, Samsung restored to sign Wi-Fi, itel remained on the normal router. Existing reports were retained.
physical.manualReconnect: Final APK: after explicit Disconnect, Live Reconnect display reused the saved credential and showed the animated Display connected confirmation with Return to Live; no password re-entry or setup navigation was required.

performance.device: itel S667LN, Flutter profile mode, eight scripted Live-screen swipes
performance.interpretation: Indicative traces show reduced framework rebuild/layout work. They are not a controlled benchmark: screen content changed, GPU slow frames remain, and no universal smoothness guarantee is made. Distribution now uses release mode.

remainingLimits: Controller program changes still briefly blink; the autonomous countdown itself remains smooth.
Automatic recovery requires the app/native service to remain running and the sign network to be reachable. Force-stop, power loss and prolonged/uncertain sessions require review.
Pairing needs peer-reachable Wi-Fi; app changes cannot override the sign hotspot's forwarding restrictions.
Controller administration mutations and long-duration endurance remain physically unverified.
Installed prototype signing key is retained for upgrade compatibility and is not a production distribution identity.
